sky: S1 = no (a safe win never leaves unfought), S2 = nearest entry, S3 = run (brief 059 'Sky's calls on S1-S3', 2026-10-25). s1-rulings.json stands; this file adds to it.

The 2026-10-25 run's 'SHIPS' (results/final-check.txt, ablation.txt, matrix2.txt, s1demo.txt) rests on two switches that are not the GDD: PROBE_SHIELD (Vale counts as cover for his carrier) and PROBE_DRAWNBREAK=1 (a drawn crew breaks at its first man down). Both are rejected here (M059-B5, M059-B6) and every number below is measured without them. DRAWNBREAK was split (2 = only 'a broken crew never presses', M059-B3); probe.ts plays the steps that compose when a plan doesn't, and logs why; PROBE_BLKHOLD was added for open item 1.

howToRead: As s1-rulings.json: kind value | rule | fix | data | keep | rejected | reference; key is a proposal and Keel names the final path; every entry is proposed: true until Sky plays it. Times m:ss.s on the mission clock; T is the run's mission Trail (the check adds campaign and cases); St is Standing at the end (start +2). 'board' = down the blocker, board, Go; 'fight out' = break the crew, then Go.

verdicts.what: Loud against the carry, at the square and at the yard
verdicts.verdict: holds: loud is dearer than the quiet carry on T, Alert, Standing and the seal at both stands

numbers.square: loud (re-composed as loud-x4: the Scout and Fixer drop 3 of the 4 drawn rivals before the carry, as §06's more-than-half break asks) wins at 5:20.1, T 27 (+3 case = 30 in the check), A 2, Standing -1, seal clock running, nobody captured. The quiet carries at the square: route-a 4:35.6 T 5 A 1 St +3; route-a-pressure 3:20.5 T 7 A 1 St +2; route-g (focus fire) 4:11.5 T 6 A 1 St +3. MC-2 and MC-10 ok: quiet 3-11 T, A <= 1, Standing >= 2; loud 30 T, A 2, Standing -1 (cand-r).

Route B's quiet carry: 7:32.6 T 3 A 0 St +3. No loud leak at the yard: MC-13's loud-wait twin is held.
numbers.why loud moved: 0.31's loud broke a single crew gun; on 0.32 gunfire at 2:31 brings the whole rival car to the Office front (2:53.2) with four on foot, who press the Enforcer when they see Vale taken. Three must go down (+4 T each, traced before the fight): loud costs 27 T against 14-15 before 059. It stays a last resort, not a route.

entries.key: fight.safe.crew: the fight body's start (Game.JoinFight, GameCrew.cs)
entries.value: A crew member who becomes a safe-fight body starts where he stands: read MemberPos(m, Tick) and SpotFor(m, st) before m.H and m.Fight are set. 0.32.0 sets them first, so MemberPos returns the new body's position (0,0) for every posted or walking member (GameCrew.cs: `m.H = h; m.Fight = true;` then `h.At = MemberPos(m, Tick)`; MemberPos answers m.H.Pos when m.Fight).
entries.reason: An engine fault, not a rule change: M059-4.1 already says they fight from where they are. It voids the safe fight in Keel's missions-check-0.32 and route-diff-0.32: route-g-board 'wins' at 4:11.5 with the blocker out 2.0 s after the spring because the posted three open from (0,0); with the fix three of them shoot the carrying Enforcer and the at-will carry is lost at both stands. Every number in this file has the fix.

entries.key: the final fight's reference fire (Waymark's compositions; no engine change)
entries.value: From the spring (safe) or fight.loud (loud), the cell's free guns lock first the blocker or the Enforcer's nearest shooter, then the next; panic covers the rest. Fight out needs more than half down (3 of 5 at the square, 2 of 3 at the yard). Loud locks 3 of the 4 drawn rivals before the carry.
entries.reason: On the fixed engine the at-will carry is lost at both stands: 3 of 5 (square) or all 3 (yard) take the carrying Enforcer as target, and §06's accumulator lands every first shot at 562 per mille. GDD §06: 'the Enforcer can't run, so the others support him'. The locks are that support and restore c037's times (route-g-board 4:11.5, route-g-fast-board 3:11.0, route-b 7:32.6). Pause is a tool: the posted three are in view before the spring.

Re-measured on 0.32: leak (a) is open with the gate off (apy-leak 2:32.0, gfy-leak 2:22.5, unfought) and closed with it (held to the blocker's down at 3:03.5). The late spring picks the blocker at the first step-out (2:51.3 at the yard). Leak (b), the floor, was not re-run on 0.32: Keel's S1-FLOOR-* scenarios measure it on his build.

entries.key: M059-4.4(c) restated (rulings.json; MC-11's yard reading, Vantage's spot check)
entries.value: At the service-drive stand, the ambush spot with the shortest grid walk to the blocker's post (the stand's blocker) reaches it within the carry and Board from Vale's rear door: 6.5 s (the 3.5 m carry, 2.5 s, plus Board carrying, 4 s), so at the blocker's walk of 1.6 m/s at most 10.4 m. Supersedes (c)'s 'at most 8 m by walk (5 s)'. The limit is read from the rules (carry pace, fight board-carrying, the hostile walk), never a fixed metre count.
entries.reason: (c)'s reason was always the time: the blocker is in the lane by the time the cell could board and go. With the gate (M059-S1.2) nothing leaks if he is late, so (c) is now about readability: by the time the Enforcer is in, the man holding the car stands where the cell can see and answer him. Measured: 9.16 m / 5.7 s on the exported lane, 7.49 m / 4.7 s on the lane from the car (M059-B10); both hold. 8 m could not hold with route B on the exported lane: every spot tried inside 8.4 m loses it (Vantage).

entries.key: getaway exit lane at a stand whose car stands on a drive (the service-drive stand); the blocker's post follows
entries.value: PROPOSED, needs Sky's yes on the GDD wording (brief 059 'Motive: the units slip, (c) and the yard's lane post (2026-10-26)'); not in the rules until then. The exit lane starts at the car and follows the getaway route: along the drive at the drive's width (3 m) to where the route meets its first road's centreline, then that carriageway at the road's width, 30 m in all; each part has square ends. The blocker's open post (lane centreline 10 m along) is then 10 m from the car on every stand: at the yard (79.35, -15.0), the drive's mouth. A stand at a kerbside bay (the square) is unchanged: its lane already starts at the car's foot.
entries.reason: §06 states the post's reason: 10-13 m from the car, 'beyond the hold and point blank, inside the cell's effective reach'; the engine checks the same (fight.blockNear > hold, blockFar < the pistol's effective reach) and LanePointAt is written as 'from the car's foot'. The exported lane starts on Apron Road 16.65 m out, so the post is 19.42 m from the car, out of the cell's reach. Measured (svc-ambush-1 at (77.35, -8.0), R): on the exported lane no plan that goes for the blocker wins (ylA, ylB: rivals-reach-vale 7:33.0), so every yard win breaks the crew (Standing +3) and §06's choice at the car (board and go, the fight moves Standing 0, or fight it out) is gone at the yard; a rival standing in the drive 8-16.65 m ahead of the car, its only way out, doesn't hold it. On the lane from the car: board and go composes (ylA: blocker down 7:28.0, Go 7:31.9, St +2, no break); fight it out unchanged (rb-ff 7:32.2, St +3); the early yard routes Go 7.1 s sooner (apy-1, gfy-1 3:00.3 against 3:07.4: the late car's blocker posts in reach and is down at 2:56.4); loud-yard unchanged (held and lost 7:42.5). The cost is route-b-board's slack: 3 s -> 0 s with today's locks (rbb-ff), 2 s re-composed (ylB: the Scout locks the blocker so he answers her, the Fixer locks rival-1 then rival-2; or ylF: the Tech steps out), against 3-4 s on the exported lane; the spot doesn't move it (2 s at three other spots). Rival-tail (90.5, -17) stays outside the lane only with the drive at its own width: at the road's 12 m it falls inside (M059-4.4(d)). MC-0..12 otherwise identical to cand-c5 (only route-b-board's line moves).

open: For Aster (a GDD/rulebook mismatch, not resolved here): GDD §06 says hostiles advance 'firing nothing while they move', and the blocker 'walks there without stopping or firing'. The rulebook and engine since 0.15.0 have hostiles firing as they walk, at walking pips (my brief 027 tuning.md §8.3; Sky 2026-10-21). Measured at the yard (PROBE_BLKHOLD, a walking blocker holding fire): at today's svc-ambush-1 it gives the same 3 s as M059-B4; with the point moved it adds nothing, so B4 doesn't depend on the answer. The GDD wins on conflict, so the GDD text or the engine needs a call.
Keel's missions-check-0.32 and route-diff-0.32 safe-fight numbers are on the (0,0) fault (M059-B1). Read them after the fix.

Robustness dropped with 059's fight: the late-step slack is 3 s for route-b-board (with M059-B4) and 1 s for route-g-fast-board, against c037's 66 s and 19 s on 0.31. The c037 fights had the crew lying in wait at fixed spots, and the pickup had no yard ambush. Part of it is the probe's locks, named by rival id, which a shifted run can misfit.
